newsitem.title: CHINA: China seeks more independent accountants.
newsitem.headline: China seeks more independent accountants.

text.p: China has moved to boost the independence of accountants involved in the securities business by ordering them to cut their links with affiliated work units, an official said on Tuesday.

Most of the 105 accountancy units in the sector had been set up by government departments involved in taxation, auditing or finance, the official from the China Institute of Certified Public Accountants said.
The new regulations aimed to boost international confidence in China's accountants, he said.
"If they are separate, accountancy offices will be more objective and fair," he said.
Accountancy in other sectors should also become more independent and government departments should not demand management fees or shares of profits from auditors, he said but gave no details.
From now until the end of 1998, China would carry out a review of its accountancy sector, the China Securities newspaper said.
All accountants in the securities sector were also being required to pass a qualifying exam, the China Securities said.
In an initial batch of exams, 431 out of 1,177 applicants had qualified, the newspaper said.
China has been keen to boost the image of its accountants, many of whom have long been subject to intense pressure from their employers and clients to present financial results in a favourable light.
Beijing recently gained membership of the International Accounting Standards Committee, which sets rules to unify accounting standards worldwide, and the International Federation of Accountants.
China promulgated its first set of rules on the auditing of listed firms at the beginning of 1996 and a second set on January 1 this year.
